guide.title: Living design system
guide.subtitle: Every colour, every size and every contrast ratio on this page comes out of the token generator. What is shown here is exactly what gets printed in the Activity 4 style guide.
guide.source: Single source: docs/entregables/estilo/uxdoc.sty. Derivation runs one way only and nothing flows back.
guide.generatedProse: Token names, usage notes and contrast rules are published in Spanish because they come from the single source of the deliverable, which is a Spanish document. The rest of the interface follows the chosen language.

entry.heading: Style guide
entry.description: Palette, typography, components and iconography of the portal, generated from the same source as the Activity 4 document. It is not a prototype: it is the system the seven of them are built with.

palette.description: Four families of five steps, seven neutrals, four semantic tokens and six chart series colours. The hexadecimal you read is the one the generator emitted: not a single one is typed here.
palette.anchorHint: Colour already versioned in uxdoc.sty since Activity 1
palette.unsupported: This browser grants no clipboard access: the value stays written in plain sight so it can be copied by hand.
palette.title: Palette
palette.noClipboard: This browser gives no clipboard access: select the value by hand.

typography.description: Two families served from this origin and nine roles. The type on this screen is the type of the document, so the specimen cannot lie.
typography.specimen: Pack my box with five dozen liquor jugs. 0123456789
typography.weightNote: All nine roles weigh 400: hierarchy is built with size, colour and white space, never with faux bold.

family.sans: Fira Sans, for body copy and figures

buttons.description: Three variants by five states, plus the destructive action and the loading one. Seventeen cells, because a matrix with holes is the fastest way for two screens to disagree.
buttons.frozenNote: Hover, focus and pressed states are shown frozen: it is the only way to capture them on a plate.
buttons.rule: One primary action per screen and no more. Amber is never a button: it informs, it does not call to action.
buttons.focusRing: The focus ring is one and the same across the product, and this plate publishes it literally: the very ring the real controls paint, minus the focus-visible variant when it is frozen.

fields.description: Six field states, five status chips and the role badges. The border uses the strong neutral: it is the fourth finding of the matrix and the reason the matrix exists.
fields.borderNote: The field border reaches 4.55:1 over the surface. The light rule stays at 1.42:1 and cannot delimit a field, only separate blocks.
fields.badgeNote: The role badge is the only documented exception to the radius scale: it uses the full radius.
fields.help: Accepted format: four digit ledger key.
fields.error: The amount must be greater than zero.

tables.description: Fixed header, alternating rows, tabular figures aligned to the right and sort order announced through aria-sort. Every numeric column of Karisma Data looks like this.
tables.caption: Recent exports by source, with synthetic demo figures
tables.sortHint: A sortable header announces its state through aria-sort, not only with an arrow: an arrow on its own never reaches a screen reader.

empty.title: No results
empty.body: No source matches the filter. Drop one filter to widen the search.

cards.description: The indicator card with its four unhappy states and the assistant tool call card with its four moments. No figure ever appears without a query behind it.

state.loadingBody: The indicator is being computed. The skeleton keeps the height of the figure so the card does not jump when the value lands.
state.emptyBody: There are no movements in the chosen period. Widen the date range.

state.forbiddenBody: Your profile does not reach this source. Access is requested from Administration.

toolCall.title: Assistant tool call card
toolCall.note: The four states are always visible: the assistant announces the query before running it, and an answer with no query behind it carries no figures.

body.announced: Query declared before it runs. It can still be stopped.
body.running: Reading the semantic layer. Step 3 of 5.
body.done: 5 rows read from the treasury catalogue.
body.error: The source did not answer. The reply carries no figures because no query returned any.

icons.description: An inventory by function, not by shape. Each icon is named after what it does in the portal and carries its own accessible name.
icons.family: A single Lucide family. No hand drawn SVG and no emoji used as a structural icon.
icons.sizes: Three sizes: 16 px in a table cell, 20 px in a button or a chip, 24 px in a card heading.
icons.label: {name}, {size} pixels

accessibility.description: The contrast matrix does not illustrate the system: it corrects it. Four combinations that were taken for granted fell below the minimum, and all four changed token.
accessibility.findings: The four defects the matrix found
accessibility.verdictLegend: The verdict is printed exactly as the generator emits it: AAA, AA, AA-grande, which means large text only from 18 px up, and falla, which means it fails.
accessibility.failures: {total} token breaks the rule it declares | {total} tokens break the rule they declare

ceiling.oscuro: Worst separation between two semantic marks, simulating protanopia, deuteranopia and tritanopia. Above 20 they are told apart by colour; even so, all of them carry a shape and an icon.
ceiling.claro: Worst separation between two semantic marks under simulated dichromacy. It is a measured ceiling, not a lack of effort: over a light ground all four semantics must clear 4.5:1, which caps them below 0.16 luminance, and four hues do not separate inside that band. That is why colour never travels alone: a reader with protanopia tells an error from a warning by the cross and the triangle.

type.title: Typography
type.rationale: The previous scale had nine roles and a single weight: the page measured 750 of 750 text nodes at weight 400, headings included, and a title to body ratio of 1.71. With size as the only channel and steps of 1.2, no jump read as a jump. Weight is a channel now: 400 for running text, 500 for labels and figures, 600 for headings.

lineage.description: Each hop states where the figure came from, what was done to it, who answers for it and how long it stays valid. The final figure never appears without its source.

origen.title: Source system
origen.transform: Untransformed. The figure as the source publishes it.

ingesta.title: Ingestion
ingesta.transform: Currency conversion at close and cancelled positions dropped.

transformacion.title: Semantic layer
transformacion.transform: Summed by business unit, memorandum accounts excluded.

publicacion.title: Published figure
publicacion.transform: Untransformed. This is what the screen shows.

conflict.title: When two systems disagree
conflict.rule: The canonical source is always named. Staying silent about the discrepancy is what sends the reader back to email, which is exactly the problem this portal exists to remove.

lineage.rationale: This plate exists because the design review flagged that "View lineage" was a button label with nothing specified behind it. A system documenting five status chips and no way to defend a figure fails the profile whose job is to answer for it.

toolCall.announce: Query announced before the data is in.

form.filtersHint: Write column=value, separate several values with commas and several filters with semicolons, for example divisa=MXN,USD; unidad_negocio=banca. Leave it empty to export the whole dataset.
form.filtersInvalid: The filter cannot be read. Every pair is written as column=value.

format.xlsxRowLimit: The Excel workbook takes up to 200,000 rows; past that cap the job ends as failed. CSV has no cap, and it is the only format that gets the million rows of Liquidity out.

job.stalled: The portal stopped hearing from this job and no longer asks about it. Request the export again.

error.missingSource: The data source is not available on the server.
error.unknownColumn: One of the filters names a column the dataset does not have.
error.formatUnavailable: The file could not be written in the requested format. The Excel workbook takes up to 200,000 rows: if the dataset is larger, narrow the filters or ask for the export as CSV, which has no cap.
error.internalFailure: The extraction failed because of an internal error of the portal.

link.expired: The link already expired. Request the export again to get a fresh one.
